impact: A read-only gate worker inherited someone else's abandoned half-codemod; an uncaught run would have reported a red gate against Epic 2 for an Epic 6 refactor that had already landed correctly.
resolution: Diff saved to scratchpad (preexisting-wip-pcgen-import-refactor.patch) before git checkout -- restored the 15 named paths; confirmed superseded by ea1a61e672 and 60fdeeb6ec after the fast-forward
summary: The re-gate worker's worktree was handed to it already dirty: 15 tracked Rust files carried an uncommitted partial codemod repointing formula_interpreter / formula_reproduction_harness imports from rules_core::pilot_compute to crate::pcgen_import, targeting modules that did not exist at that SHA. Left in place the tree would not compile and every stage after the first cargo stage would have failed for a reason unrelated to the epic under gate. The same refactor later landed properly as ea1a61e672 / 60fdeeb6ec (AT-35-E6-001), so the WIP was superseded dead work, not lost work.

reason: This worker runs under a worktree-isolation guard that refuses any git invocation naming a path outside its own worktree, so git worktree remove / git rev-list on the 13 sibling worktrees is not available to it at all. It can measure them (14 worktrees, 606M-887M each, 11.3G total) but cannot prove unmerged-ness or remove them. Removing an unmerged or dirty worktree blind is the one thing the standing rule forbids. Disk is not pressing: 420G free, 72% used, well under scripts/reclaim.sh's threshold. The two Epic 2 worktrees the first re-gate identified (wf_291be5c8-5f3-14 at a542652c5e, wf_291be5c8-5f3-15 at 8cc4ea1516) were already retained by that gate because git worktree remove refused them for modified/untracked files; nothing has changed that.

detected_by: scripts/verify.sh stage site-dashboard-check -> exit 1; /tmp/codex-verify-FYQLkl/site-dashboard-check.log: line 1 'input pin matches docs/work-inventory.json (5a0a0787312b5181d41214cb52abcd6e0c250fc409a75675ed6e839b4142e36f)', line 2 'site/dashboard/PF1e-dashboard.json is STALE'
impact: Epic 2's re-gate cannot return green; workflow-instruction.md §10 step 0 owes a wrap-up correction cycle before the next epic's second cycle dispatches. Fourth firing of a key whose control (republish when the inventory moves) demonstrably does not cover this shape.
summary: FOURTH firing in the SD-35 window. Full verify.sh at f1f547a41e: 48 of 49 stages PASS, site-dashboard-check FAIL. This firing has a NEW sub-mechanism the existing key does not describe: site-dashboard-pin PASSED (docs/work-inventory.json still hashes to the pin the feed was published from), so the dominant input did NOT move. The feed was republished one commit earlier, in 6e4b1f7b4e (the Epic 5 wrap-up correction, whose own stated fix was 'the stale feed republished'), and the only commit above it is f1f547a41e, a docs-only receipt. A feed that goes STALE with its input pin intact and one docs commit above its own republish is drifting on something other than work-inventory.

actual: The published feed is genuinely, badly wrong, and the drift is confined entirely to work_inventory doneness aggregates. Committed feed: by_doneness done=23650 in-progress=17563. Fresh strict render from the SAME pinned docs/work-inventory.json: done=46965 in-progress=160. All 650 differing paths are under /work_inventory (by_doneness, by_doneness_book_kind, books[*].by_doneness); channels, content_state, matrix, manifests, unit_index, books and workchannels are byte-identical after the standard scrub. The public site has been understating SD-35's headline by ~23,300 units. ROOT CAUSE: publish-site-dashboard.sh's publish branch runs the producer WITHOUT PF1E_DASHBOARD_STRICT_TIMEOUT=1 (only --check sets it), so a state dump that times out silently falls back to a stale cache, and write_input_pin then stamps that stale render as authoritative in the same run. The pin therefore certifies the INPUT, never that the published OUTPUT was rendered from it, which is why site-dashboard-pin passes while site-dashboard-check fails.
claimed: The published feed is current (site-dashboard-pin PASS), and the STALE verdict is drift in a non-repo-derived subtree such as channels or retrospective that the --check scrub does not drop
